nit: Please put into a details sub-namespace so it is clear(er) this is not an external API.
yep.  On the list to move to the utility namespace.
Moved to utility namespace, and moved the helper method to details.

This doesn't actually give a tuple<foo&, bar&>, does it?  It gives a tuple<foo, bar>.

https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/utility/tuple/make_tuple

> For each Ti in Types..., the corresponding type Vi in VTypes... is std::decay<Ti>::type unless application of std::decay results in std::reference_wrapper<X> for some type X, in which case the deduced type is X&.
Yep, This was me moving to a real qemu build to test the options between std::tie and std::reference_wrapper.

std::tie seems like what we want here.  Current code uses it.

I'm still not clear on std::tie vs std::tuple, but there's unit tests that prove that we got it right.
lgtm
will look at the ci fail tomorrow

I found a formatting thing and 

```
../test/message/call.cpp:69: Failure
Expected equality of these values:
  syncBusId(b)
    Which is: "10a7264c79351b42987b0cbe68dddedf"
  id
    Which is: ""
```

Which I don't think is related to this change.  It looks like there's a 1 second sleep that might not have been enough and the machine was under load?
feel free to just tell me "no" 😊

> but goto isn't unreasonable for this

Unfortunately, the coding standard disagrees with you on that 😊

https://isocpp.github.io/CppCoreGuidelines/CppCoreGuidelines#Res-goto

the goal with this structure was as you saw, to avoid duplicating the std::apply call.  Technically both paths are "happy" paths, just one involves not reading params on an error return.

I appreciate the input, but I'm going to go ahead and decline because one of the "rules" in asio is one wait should result in exactly one callback.  That's easy to verify in this flow, because there is literally only one callback.  If we duplicate, that's harder to "see" even if it's correct.
Done
